correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication yields the exact 2×2 block [[−ab,a],[b,0]]; Gaussian rotational symmetry and conditioning yield independent G/sqrt(chi-square_s) slopes. Independent beta reciprocal factors give the full distribution, integral CDF and Mellin transform, including the s=2 divergent mean square boundary. For log-inverse-beta variables the convolution has e^(−αz)(z+O(1))/B² density because the endpoint excess kernel is integrable, proving the exact power-log coefficient; identity-side specialization proves the one-sided comparison. Verified against 3221 standalone source-program assertions. Numerical tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: An actual theorem-to-theorem comparison against the motivating 2026 article and several older primary works showed qualitative/conditional oblique errors, embedding bounds, different random oblique CUR/OLS estimators, or orthogonal residual projection expectations, but no result implying the full independent-beta-product law, exact finite-sample CDF, critical moments and sharp two-sided log-tail versus one-sided power-tail contrast. The raw beta-ratio and convolution identities are known methods and are not claimed independently. The historical-priority conclusion is conditional on accessible evidence; older special-function and numerical sketching results remain possible.
residual_risks: A generic pre-existing exact product-of-beta distribution formula may supply the logarithmic coefficient abstractly; independent priority of the operator-specific application has not been established exhaustively.
Stewart 2011 and all older specialized projector papers were not available for full-text line-by-line comparison.
